references.text: Repeats the prohibition against sexual intercourse between men and specifies the death penalty as a consequence. Uses the same terminology with 'תועבה' (abomination).
The account of Sodom, where the men of the city sought to have sexual relations with the male guests. This has traditionally been linked to the prohibition in Leviticus.
A similar incident in Gibeah, where men sought to have sexual relations with a male guest, described as a shameful act.
Refers to temple prostitution and male prostitutes ('קדשים') in the land, which is associated with the Canaanite abominations.
King Asa removed the male temple prostitutes from the land as part of his religious reform.
Paul describes men who abandoned natural relations with women and burned with desire for one another, calling this shameful.
Paul mentions 'ἀρσενοκοῖται' (men who lie with men) in a list of those who will not inherit the kingdom of God.
Mentions 'ἀρσενοkoῖται' as one of the sins the law was given to counteract.
